candidates.title: First look: CPKC earnings
candidates.excerpt: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported a 16% increase in third-quarter core adjusted earnings per share Wednesday, as higher freight volumes and growth in grain and intermodal revenue helped offset rising fuel costs. Revenue rose to C$4.22 billion ($3.01 billion) in the three months ended Sept. 30 from $2.61 billion a year earlier, the Calgary-based company (NYSE: CP) said in earnings released after the close of markets. candidates.title: Greenbrier profit falls as railcar demand weighs on sales
candidates.excerpt: Greenbrier Cos. reported a sharp decline in quarterly profit and revenue as the freight-railcar manufacturer contended with weaker demand and facility-related costs. The Lake Oswego, Ore., company (NYSE: GBX) saw an increase in its order backlog and growth in its leasing fleet amid improving business conditions. The company said Monday that net earnings attributable to Greenbrier fell to $8.7 million, or 27 cents a diluted share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Aug. 31, from $36.8 million, or $1.16 a share, a year earlier. Revenue declined 22% to $591 million from $759.5 million. Excluding facility-rationalization costs, core earnings were 39 cents a share. The charges reduced quarterly earnings by 12 cents a share after tax and non-controlling interests. Revenue fell short of analysts’ expectations of about $605 million, while core earnings missed the 80-cent analysts’ consensus of MarketBeat. Earnings per share grew 3%, to 74 cents. The railway’s operating ratio was 64.8%, a 1.3-point increase over a year ago as expenses climbed 18% largely due to higher fuel costs. Volume was up 5% when measured by carloads and containers, or 6% on the basis of revenue ton-miles, which is CPKC’s preferred metric. candidates.title: News photos:  Connecticut breaks ground for new station on CTrail Hartford Line
candidates.excerpt: News photos: Connecticut breaks ground for new station on CTrail Hartford Line News photos: Connecticut breaks ground for new station on CTrail Hartford Line By Scott A. Hartley | October 28, 2026 New Enfield station will be built at site of former New Haven Station last served by Amtrak in 1986 ENFIELD, Conn. — Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont was among officials on hand today (Oct. 28) for a ceremonial groundbreaking for a new CTrail station in Enfield. The structure will be built on the site of the former New Haven Railroad Thompsonville station, last served by Amtrak in 1986. Others on hand included Lt. Gov. Susan Bysiewicz, Transportation Commissioner Garrett Eucalitto, U.S. Sen. Richard Blumenthal, U.S. Rep. Joe Courtney, and local elected officials. The station is slated to open in early 2030 following construction, as well as track and bridge work. It is adjacent to housing in the former Bigelow-Sanford carpet mill, and will serve new residential units currently under construction.

candidates.title: Weekly U.S. rail traffic up again
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Continued strength in intermodal traffic led to another increase in U.S. rail volume for the week ending Oct. 24, 2026. According to statistics from the Association of American Railroads, volume for the week was 538,503 carloads and intermodal units, up 7.8% from the same week a year ago. The overall figure included 234,826 carloads, up 3.6%, and 303,677 containers and trailers, an increase of 11.3%. For the year to date, cumulative volume is 21,601,184 carloads and intermodal units, an increase of 3.8% compared with the first 42 weeks of 2025. The 9,609,543 carloads are an increase of 2.7%, while the 11,991,641 intermodal units are up 4.7%. North American traffic for the week, as reported by nine U.S., Canadian, and Mexican railroads, was 739,068 carloads and intermodal units, up 8% from the corresponding week in 2025. CSX freight traffic was down sharply, according to RailState, which monitors rail traffic with a trackside sensor network. RailState sensors cover CSX’s northern tier as well as points in Florida and the St. Louis area. “CSX freight traffic is down 60% against its 30-day average,” RailState said, based on the 21 hours between 7 p.m. Tuesday and 4:40 p.m. today. candidates.title: Union Pacific posts record third-quarter revenue and profits
candidates.excerpt: Union Pacific reported record third-quarter revenue and profits as higher volume, pricing, and efficiency gains more than offset the impact of rising fuel prices and inflation. “Union Pacific’s third-quarter results demonstrate our ability to safely deliver the service we sold our customers while efficiently handling 6% volume growth,” Chief Executive Jim Vena said on the railroad’s (NYSE: UNP) earnings call today. Operating income increased 15%, to $2.94 billion, as revenue grew 15%, to $7.19 billion. Earnings per share rose 16%, to $3.49. The railroad’s operating ratio was 59.1%, a 0.1-point improvement compared to a year ago. Workforce productivity, measured by car-miles per employee, improved 5%. Overall volume was up 6% for the quarter. Premium volume — which includes intermodal and automotive traffic — was up 9%. candidates.title: First look: Union Pacific earnings
candidates.excerpt: Union Pacific reported a 16% increase in third-quarter profit Thursday as higher freight volumes, pricing gains and fuel surcharges lifted revenue, with intermodal traffic leading the railroad’s growth. The Omaha-based railroad (NYSE: UNP) earned $2.08 billion, or $3.49 per diluted share, compared with $1.79 billion, or $3.01 per share, a year earlier. Adjusted earnings of $3.53 per share exceeded the $3.47 consensus estimate compiled by Zacks Investment Research. Operating revenue increased 15% to $7.2 billion, while freight revenue excluding fuel surcharges rose 6%. Total revenue carloads grew 6% to 2.29 million. Intermodal volume increased 11% to 956,000 containers and trailers, and intermodal revenue climbed 27% to $1.52 billion.
